OBJECT OF THE CALL
  Predict the near-session environment for the SECTOR ETF named in the sector layer

CHANNEL 1 (injected by pipeline — trust these numbers)

  Plus sector ETF vs SPY relative returns (1d/3d/1w/1m).

CHANNEL 2 (your job — always cover before scoring)
  1. Shared macro regime as it hits THIS sector (risk-on/off, real yields, USD)
  2. Sector SPINE factors (defined in the sector layer — mandatory)
  3. Sector secondary factors (taxonomy checklist)
  4. Breadth / leadership inside the sector
  5. Flows / positioning / crowding for the sector ETF or peers
  6. Earnings/guidance or policy catalysts for the sector

COMPONENT SCORES (pipeline parses SECTOR_SCORES block)

  S1_SECTOR_FACTORS (−3..+3): net of spine + secondary HITs (specialized list in sector layer)
  S2_BREADTH (−2..+2): expansion vs ETF-only / mega-name carry
  S3_FLOWS_POSITIONING (−2..+2): inflows, outflows, crowding, forced flows
  S4_ETF_TAPE (−1..+1): CONFIRMATION ONLY from Channel 1 relative returns — never the main thesis
  MULTIPLIER (0.5–2.0), CONFIDENCE (0–1), REGIME (risk_on|risk_off|mixed)

OUTPUT
  Line 1: MEMORY_CONFIRM: ...
  Free analysis Markdown
  SECTOR_SCORES_BEGIN ... SECTOR_SCORES_END (exact keys)
  Optional HIT_GRID_BEGIN ... END with label|status|confidence|date|url

### a-sector-etf-gaps-up-1-at-the-open-on-the-back-of-a-multi-da.md
## RULE
(1) On a gap-up open, prior-session relative tape is already in the price — score S4=0, not +1, and do not re-score the same fact in S2. (2) When the sector's own shock is day-3+ with no fresh increment and the incremental commodity print is sub-1.5%, S1 caps at +1 (not +2) — the prose and the score must agree. (3) The magnitude-discipline rule must be enforced at the scoring layer: if the narrative says "cap at mild," the pipeline must not emit notable; a written cap the arithmetic can override is not a cap. (4) Run the knowable-at-open test explicitly: if every bullish item is already-printed and the only forward item is two-sided (EIA WPSR), the base case is a gap fade, not a continuation.

## WHEN IT FIRES
A sector ETF gaps up ≥1% at the open on the back of a multi-day shock that is now on day-3+ with no fresh step-change headline, in a risk-off broad tape, after a large 1m relative run (≥+8%); the model scores prior-session relative tape (Channel 1 through the prior close) as live forward confirmation in both the breadth channel (S2) and the ETF-tape channel (S4), and scores the sector-factor cluster (S1) at +2 despite its own prose calling it a "modest continuation" w …

### a-sector-etf-sits-at-near-all-time-highs-after-a-multi-week.md
## RULE
(1) Treat a record-close sequence (e.g. 12th record close since end-July) plus 1m rel ≥ +8% as a live crowded-long condition on its own — do not gate the crowding trigger on 1w rel >+5%. (2) Apply a marginal-increment asymmetry test: when the sector's own factor moves only sub-1.5% d/d while the sector is at records, net S1 toward 0/+1 rather than +2, because the marginal equity upside is small and the profit-taking downside at records is large. (3) Do not score S2 and S4 both positive off the same prior-close Channel 1 series — cap the combined breadth+tape contribution at +1. (4) Score S3 negative (crowded-long unwind risk) when a record-high sector with a multi-week run and a flow hangover faces only a small incremental factor move. (5) The pipeline-computed decision must honor the prose magnitude cap — emitting "notable" against a prose "mild" is a scoring-integrity failure.

## WHEN IT FIRES
A sector ETF sits at/near all-time highs after a multi-week relative run (1m rel strongly positive, e.g. ≥ +8%) with a sequence of record closes, while the sector's own fundamental driver (crude/geopolitical premium) is still green but its *incremental* move is small (sub-1.5% d/d) …

### sector-etf-prediction-where-the-prior-session-had-a-1-relati.md
## RULE

### sector-prediction-calls-flat-flat-when-the-sector-s-own-fact.md
## RULE
When S1 is a live, verified sector-factor print (oil offered −1.19% WTI / −1.07% Brent) and S4 is 0 only because the prior session's 1d relative move was flat (not because the current session's premarket tape is confirming strength), the model should emit a signed direction (down/mild or down/notable depending on magnitude rules) rather than flat. A flat prior-day tape is not a counter-signal to a live offered barrel; it is a neutral starting point. The DO-INSTEAD rule should only fire when the live tape is actually flat/mixed at the decision time (e.g., premarket XLE flat, majors mixed), not when the prior session's close was flat. Additionally, the crowded-long condition (1w rel +4.40%, 1m rel +12.04%) combined with a live offered barrel is a fade setup, not a reason to downgrade to flat — extension increases downside risk on a factor reversal, it does not neutralize it.

The flat band requires either (a) mixed signs across components, (b) a single negative component without tape confirmation, or (c) sub-threshold negative evidence (rel between −0.5% and −1.5%).

## WHEN IT FIRES
